pairs.why: Nearly identical red hatboxes with the same matte finish, twisted rope and soft green-backdrop lighting; neither one is clearly closer to the real cards.
Both match in finish, but B has a tiny gold crown decal on the lid that looks lifted from the phone-booth reference, while A is a cleaner, believable object.
A has a slightly taller drum and B has a stray crown mark on the lid, but the rendering, color and light are the same, so neither gives the card away more.
The only differences are tiny ones in the grommets and lid emblem; both have the same soft, slightly matte game-card finish.
B's rope is smooth and tube-like, which reads more like a molded toy (the statue-like look the lessons rejected), while A's twisted rope reads as a real material, like the real cards' detailing.
A's handle is a smooth plastic-looking tube, while B's twisted rope gives the built, real-material detail the real cards have.
Almost the same image: the same proportions, rope, matte red finish and lighting, with no meaningful difference.
B's lid is a bit wider and has a faint crown mark, but the finish, color and light are the same as A's, and both could pass equally.
